source_message.speaker: freelancer
source_message.text: Also, fitting everything within the given dimensions of the main board is not possible.

execution.observed_behavior: The specified main-board components and connectors cannot fit within the given board dimensions.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
The small board on the left is the sensors board, the middle one is the main board, and the one on the right is the power board. This is for a prototype, so I can adjust the dimensions, etc.
The key point is that, as you can see, they stand vertically. That means the cables will be easier to connect if they are on top, or on the sides in the case of smaller connectors.

source_message.speaker: freelancer
source_message.text: With those holes, routing everything properly is impossible.

execution.observed_behavior: The main-board outline and ESP32 breakout holes leave insufficient space to route everything properly.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
My rough calculation is that, on a 70×50 board (3500mm²), the components would occupy around 1300mm² (~37% coverage). That is comfortably within standard PCB density and should allow clean routing on 4 layers.

I would rather retain the separate JST connectors instead of combining them into a 2x15+10p. Modularity matters for the enclosure: every sensor has its own clean cable, and the boards slide into rails. Using one large connector with a fan-out ribbon cable would create very messy internal enclosure wiring and make servicing difficult.
Because all the components are already placed in KiCad, could you resize the board outline to 70×50 and make a rough rearrangement? I lack KiCad skills, so something that would take you minutes with the full project already open would take me hours. I would really appreciate it if you could attempt the resize on your end.

I have noted that the ESP32 needs to be on the edge, and that is fine.

routing_warnings.description: This message specifies the physical placement and alignment of connectors on the main and sensor boards rather than the main-board outline or routing capacity.
The hard requirement to retain access to every ESP32 pin belongs to the independent full-pin-breakout Requirement.

missing_requirement_candidates.description: The sensor board has a separate component-fit problem and subsequent completion claim. This trajectory is independent of the main-board form-factor Requirement and is not represented by a suitable frozen Requirement.
